Common teaching rules.\n Please fix your student\'s pronounciaction at any time and make the student repeat the correct pronounciation 3 times.\n If the student asks a question using broken English, please first correct the student\'s question and have the student repeat the question 3 times. Then answer the student\'s question. If the student uses broken English at any time during the lesson, always fix it with a correct sentence. Ask the student to repeat the correct sentence 3 times. (Just three times is enough; more repetition can make the student feel stressed!)

%s\n How to teach a Normal lesson mode\n 1. The tutor will read a phrase once; the student will repeat it three times. Repeat for all phrases. 2. Make the student read each phrase independently. 3. Hide phrases for the student by selecting the "Display sentences as ***" option from the menu button. 4. Once again, the tutor will read each phrase once and the student will repeat it back three times. Repeat for all phrases. 5. Make the student read each phrase on his/her own again. After each phrase, please rate the quality of the student\'s speaking with an A, B, or C. 6. Next, randomly select a phrase for the student to read. Do so by selecting the person icon to the left of the phrase. You can now move on to the next topic. You can do so by selecting the "Move to the next topic" option from the "Topic" menu.

%s\n How to conduct a role playing lesson\n 1. Press the "Menu" button. Select the "Change to Role Playing mode" option, then select the topic to role play. Ask the student which topic he/she wants to do. 2. Student - A (Tutor - B) The student will read an example sentence under the A-cell. (The student is able to see example sentences under A-cells, but not B-cells.) 3. Click the refresh button & switch roles. Tutor - A (Student - B) As a teacher, you will not see any example sentences. Please look at the cell prompt and create a simple sentence that satisfies the prompt. If a student cannot think of what to say when it is his/her turn, prompt him/her with a simple sentence of your own. Ask the student to repeat the sentence 3 times. 4. Click the refresh button & repeat roles. Tutor - A (Student - B) 5. Click the refresh button & do "listen and repeat". 6. Now, the student will read all A-cells. You will respond appropriately to the B-cell prompt. Have the student repeat your sentence once. If the student has trouble repeating your sentence, say your answer once more and have the student repeat it 3 times. 7. Ask the student if he/she would like to continue practicing this role play topic, or if he/she wants to move on to another topic.

%s\n How to do exam mode\n 1. The teacher will read the word once and the student will repeat the word 3 times. 2. While the student is repeating the word 3 times, rate the student\'s speaking (A: Good, B: Okay (ex. pronounciation is a bit off), C: Bad (it seems like the student know the word at all)). 3. The student will select the correct answer to the multiple choice question. 4. If the student\'s answer is wrong, the teacher will read the word again and have the student repeat it 3 times. 5. Repeat this for all the words in the list. 6. Once you go through all the words, go back to the "Exam" menu and select the "Except ! and A" option. When you see the question "Do you want to reuse current exam list?" pop up, select "Yes". 7. Go through the word list one more time using the same method. Once you\'ve finished, go to the "Exam" menu and select the "Change to Lesson Mode" option. From there you can move to the next topic and enter the "Exam mode" again.

The student will read role A's example sentences while the teacher will respond appropriately as role B.

The student can see examples for role A but not for role B. The teacher only sees hints to help make appropriate sentences.

Examples are not shown to teachers because we want to expose the students to various expressions that can be used in the same situation.

Students rarely have opportunities to use role A expressions in every day life so they are shown examples, but if they know how to say role A type expressions they will also be able to discern them better.
